doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Out-of-body moments and levitation at Temple University
summary: When the music flows nothing else exists; Temple audience members said the band levitated.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Earlier on when you were talking about astral projecting and out of body, have you ever had what you would describe as an out of body experience playing with either your own group or with Pharoah?

Well they told us something one time, oh yeah, when the music gets going I mean you just playing, so I mean there is no such thing as a body or whatever. I mean you’re into the music and nothing else exists. But we used to perform at a lot of the universities and one of them was in Philadelphia, was Temple University. And we did a concert one night and the people said, “I wish I had videotaped it.” They said, “We know you all were playing and you all levitated.” I said okay. “I wish I had videotaped this.” But I can’t prove it, but I mean when the music is really going and you really get into the music it’s just sound so I mean so you’re not even aware of anything else. But those are the moments that you look for, that make it worthwhile.
